Opinium for GOSH Charity, 2,000 UK adults, favorite childhood superhero (top 3 only)
sources.method: public poll, fieldwork 8-12 Dec 2023, weighted nationally representative; only Superman 18%, Batman 16%, Spider-Man 15% published

changes_vs_current: Superman moves to #1 and Batman #2 (Spider-Man #3, all three in the top 3 of every source that lists them); Captain Marvel jumps to #8 on one source (OnePoll #8); Robin/Nightwing and Hellboy enter; Black Panther falls from #10 to #18 (IGN #51 drags it down against OnePoll #9 and Vue #17) and Ant-Man and Black Widow drop out (IGN-only, #67 and #74); Wonder Woman stays #4, Iron Man #7. Rule applied: new entrants needed 2+ sources, so Jean Grey, The Thing, Professor X, Punisher and Nick Fury (IGN-only, avg 15-20) were not added.
confidence: low. Only 4 sources and three are short lists (20, 10, 3 names), so positions 13-24 rest mainly on IGN's 2011 editorial list, which predates the MCU and over-rates comics-only characters while under-rating Black Panther, Doctor Strange, Black Widow, Ant-Man and Hawkeye. Ranks 1-7 are solid. Hellboy and Robin are included only because the Vue poll and IGN counted them as heroes; swap in Black Widow or Ant-Man if you prefer. Wisevoter 2024 state-by-state survey, read via CBR (cbr.com/spider-man-batman-america-favorite-superhero-marvel-dc), gives Spider-Man #1 in 25 states, Batman 10, Superman 4, and Iron Man in the top five in 44 states, which is consistent with this order but not in the math. YouGov (2013) names Batman, Spider-Man, Superman and Wonder Woman in its top five favorite comic characters (with Archie), also consistent. Search-interest studies (Game/Looper 2021) were skipped as not polls.
